fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is high-pressure quenching of the original composition, whereas the target intervention changes Fe/Co/Mn ratios, lowers P from 20 to 15 at.%, and uses melt spinning at 40 m/s.

The claim that approximately 1 GPa necessarily raises the crystal-nucleation barrier is not thermodynamically established; pressure effects depend on liquid-to-crystal volume changes and pressure-dependent phase equilibria and may instead favor crystallization.

The asserted cooling-rate window of approximately 10^3 to at least 10^5 K/s is unsupported and does not match the reported boundaries: an ingot average of 95.9 K/s and complete amorphization only in approximately 20 μm melt-spun ribbon.
No prior evidence is cited for pressure-induced amorphization or improved reheating stability in this alloy or a relevant transition-metal phosphide system.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad objective of suppressing primary crystallization and proposes a reasonably controlled falsification experiment using matched cooling rates, XRD, microscopy, and DSC. However, it does not reconstruct the demonstrated composition adjustment or the experimentally successful melt-spinning condition. It also misses the eutectic-growth and segregation/phosphide mechanism, the 20 K/min DSC boundary, the absence of a detected glass transition, and the reported three-stage devitrification from 659 K to about 820 K. Its pressure mechanism is speculative and stated too generally without evidence or pressure-dependent phase-volume data. Thus it is novel and experimentally testable, but not adequately supported as a solution to this specific materials system.
